I fixed the issue with PR #30217 — turned out to be two unrelated bugs in the session list, both worth landing in one PR.

**Bug 1 — "Load More" is stuck.** With `directory=` set, `GET /session?offset=N&limit=L` was returning the same first page no matter what `offset` you sent. The frontend's "Load More" was effectively a no-op whenever you were scoped to a directory.

- **Root cause:** `offset` was never declared on `ListQuery`, never on `ListInput`, never read off `ctx.query` in the handler, and never applied to the database query in `listByProject` — every layer silently dropped it, so the server was always just running the same "give me the first `limit` rows" query regardless of what the client sent.
- **Fix:** plumbed `offset` through all four layers — added the field to `ListQuery` and `ListInput`, forwarded it in the handler, and added the matching `OFFSET` to the SQL so the server actually skips past the first `offset` rows.

**Bug 2 — `?roots=true` returns 500.** The v2 `Info.time.archived` field was wrapped in `optionalOmitUndefined(V2Schema.DateTimeUtcFromMillis)`, and any query that hit an archived root session blew up with `Expected DateTime.Utc, got 1780160907969`. The v1 path was fine, which is why this only surfaced on the v2 endpoint.

- **Root cause:** the v2 field wraps `DateTimeUtcFromMillis`, which is itself a schema that converts between a `number` (epoch millis) and a `DateTime.Utc` value in both directions. The bug is in how `optionalOmitUndefined` composes with that — when it builds the optional wrapper, it accidentally double-applies the number-to-DateTime conversion, so by the time the outer encoder runs it's already looking at a `number` but expecting a `DateTime.Utc` and throws. The v1 `Info.time.archived` doesn't have this problem because it wraps plain `Schema.Finite` (a number is a number, no conversion involved), so the wrapper just works as expected. Only the v2 wrapper around `DateTimeUtcFromMillis` hits the edge case.
- **Fix:** swapped the wrapper for plain `Schema.optional(...)` to match what `packages/core/src/session/message.ts` already does for `time.completed` / `time.ran` / `time.pruned`. The wire format is now identical to the bare `DateTimeUtcFromMillis` field, no observable change for working inputs.

Quick rebase status: the branch is **88 commits behind `dev`** and the conflicts ended up being non-trivial:

- `packages/opencode/src/cli/cmd/run/keymap.shared.ts` was **deleted** upstream in commit e8dd8f7 ("tui(run): use keymap instead of raw key events"). The leader-guard logic in that file is now obsolete because the run/keymap layer takes a different shape.
- `packages/opencode/src/cli/cmd/tui/keymap.tsx` has had a non-trivial refactor in `registerOpencodeKeymap`; my leader-deactivation guard (`leaderTrigger != null && (!Array.isArray(leaderTrigger) || leaderTrigger.length > 0)`) still applies cleanly on top of the new shape — I have it rebased locally and `bun test test/config/tui.test.ts` passes 41/41 on the rebased branch.
- `packages/opencode/src/cli/cmd/tui/config/tui.ts` and `packages/opencode/test/config/tui.test.ts` rebased cleanly around `dropUnknownTopLevelKeys` / unknown-top-level-key tests.

GitHub's web "Resolve conflicts" editor refuses this set (says "too complex"), and I'm pushing from a managed workstation that won't authenticate a personal-account git push right now. Will force-push the rebased branch the moment I'm back on a machine with the right creds, or happy to **close this and reopen against current `dev`** if that's easier for review. Sorry for the friction — the underlying fix and tests are unchanged.

Heads-up on this PR's status against current `dev`:

The upstream refactor in commit 7f571d3 ("refactor(core): move database schema ownership #29068") **deleted** `packages/opencode/src/storage/db.ts` — which is the file this PR patches. The WAL → DELETE fallback is still needed though; the same `PRAGMA journal_mode = WAL` calls just moved to new homes:

- `packages/core/src/database/database.ts` (Effect-style — `.pipe(Effect.catch(() => db.run("PRAGMA journal_mode = DELETE")))`)
- `packages/core/src/database/sqlite.bun.ts` (raw Bun `Database` — `try { native.run("PRAGMA journal_mode = WAL;") } catch { native.run("PRAGMA journal_mode = DELETE;") }`)
- `packages/core/src/database/sqlite.node.ts` (same shape)
- `packages/opencode/src/storage/json-migration.ts` (one-time migration still issues the WAL pragma)

I have the rewrite implemented locally on a fresh branch from current `dev` — `bun typecheck` clean in both `packages/core` and `packages/opencode`, `bun test test/storage/` passes 36/36. Two clean commits:

- `fix(core): fall back to DELETE journal mode when WAL pragma fails`
- `fix(opencode): fall back to DELETE journal mode in json migration`

Can't push from this managed workstation right now (personal-account auth not available here). Will force-push the rewrite, or happy to **close this PR and open a fresh one** against current `dev` if reviewer preference. Same underlying fix — unblocks WAL-unsupported filesystems (WSL, network mounts) without crashing startup.

Reproduced via bash aliases for me.

I have this alias set by default in my `.bashrc`: `alias ls='eza --git --git-repos'`, my ls output was blank inside OpenCode.
Removed it with a TERM=dumb condition, and it works now:
```shell
if [[ "$TERM" != "dumb" ]]; then
    alias ls='eza --git --git-repos'
fi
```

Weirdly, it only affects `ls` for me (I also have an `alias k='kubectl'` which works inside OpenCode)
